title: TAP versus the Web Bot Auth working group draft: header rules
caption: Both use RFC 9421, but TAP does not conform to draft-ietf-webbotauth-httpsig-protocol-00. TAP launched almost eleven months before the draft, so the draft is not its basis.
alt: Side-by-side comparison. TAP: tags agent-browser-auth or agent-payer-auth; covers @authority and @path; no Signature-Agent required; keyid is an opaque key id; nonce and alg required; window at most 8 minutes; keys at mcp.visa.com/.well-known/jwks. Web Bot Auth draft -00: tag web-bot-auth; covers @authority or @target-uri plus a signed Signature-Agent header, which is required; keyid is a JWK SHA-256 thumbprint; no nonce required by the draft; expiry of 24 hours or less recommended; keys at /.well-known/http-message-signatures-directory. Each pair differs.
